entries.title: Exodus 7:1
segments: I have made thee a god to Pharaoh--thy prophet; as God communicates to men his will through prophets, so Aaron should make known to Pharaoh the messages which Moses, acting in God's name, should direct him to deliver.

entries.title: Exodus 7:3
segments: Harden Pharaoh's heart; as a punishment for his sins, he was given up to hardness of heart and blindness of mind, so that God's dealings with him served only to increase his obduracy and wickedness.

entries.title: Exodus 7:4
segments: That I may lay my hand upon Egypt; this was not Pharaoh's object in refusing to obey God, but it was God's object in suffering him to do it.

entries.title: Exodus 7:5
segments:
The Egyptians shall know; that Jehovah is almighty, and able to do his pleasure. 
 
The Lord takes occasion, even from the obstinacy and wickedness of men, to manifest his character and show forth his glory, to the terror of his enemies and the joy of his friends.

entries.title: Exodus 7:11
segments: The sorcerers--the magicians; men who pretended to supernatural power, and were accustomed to practise deceits upon their fellow-men.

Pharaoh wished to see whether his own magicians could perform like wonders. 
 
  With their enchantments; certain mysterious forms of words by which they pretended to work wonders.

entries.title: Exodus 7:12
segments: And they became serpents; this was probably done by sleight of hand.

entries.title: Exodus 7:13
segments: He hardened Pharaoh's heart; this in the original is the same as in

, where it is rendered, Pharaoh's heart was hardened. 
 
Things which, in the course of divine providence, take place through the wickedness of men, are sometimes, in the Bible, ascribed to God. This shows his all-controlling agency, though he cannot be tempted, neither does he at any time tempt men to commit sin.

entries.title: Exodus 7:19
segments: Streams--rivers; the various branches of the Nile, and the canals leading from it.

entries.title: Exodus 7:22
segments: Did so with their enchantments; imitated in appearance the miracle of Moses.  As Pharaoh did not love the truth, God suffered the magicians to deceive him to a certain point by their enchantments.

Thus his heart was hardened, and he persisted in his obduracy. 
 
When men dislike to obey God, and seek excuses for their neglect, they can generally find them; and when they wish to harden themselves against him, he often suffers them to do it, even to their ruin.
